card.summary: Free deposit, no published cap. 'Is there a cost to deposit data in BioStudies? No, both deposition of data to BioStudies and data access are free of charge....

free_tier.stated: Free deposit, no published cap. 'Is there a cost to deposit data in BioStudies? No, both deposition of data to BioStudies and data access are free of charge.' Docs discuss 'larger data volumes (hundreds of GiB)' as routine.

retention.stated: Binding constraint on read is per-ip-shaping. 1 stream 7 KB/s, 16 parallel 25 KB/s against the EBI FTP edge. Retention: permanent, DOI auto-assigned; files can sit 'hold until published' indefinitely before release.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous. 'Anonymous downloads are enabled' over FTP; also HTTPS. No egress meter anywhere in the docs.

record.tooling: Submission Tool + FTP + Aspera (ascp) in; anonymous FTP/HTTPS out. Path is predictable: /biostudies/<mode>/<COLL>/<COLL0-99>/<ACC>/Files/ where mode is `fire` or `nfs`.
record.chaining: ArrayExpress is a BioStudies collection, so one account covers both. Unlimited accessions per account; each accession gets its own directory tree. Read side anonymous per-file HTTP, so it fronts to a CDN trivially.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: none stated; Aspera recommended above 10 GiB. Binding constraint on read is per-ip-shaping. 1 stream 7 KB/s, 16 parallel 25 KB/s against the EBI FTP edge. Retention: permanent, DOI auto-assigned; files can sit 'hold until published' indefinitely before release.

identity_cost.detail: depositing needs a BioStudies submission-tool account, created with a name, an email address and a password; the ORCID field is optional. No card and no phone number is asked for. Reading published data needs no account at all.

record.reliability_note: Read edge is slow per connection and stalls connections under parallel load (one of 16 timed out with 0 bytes). Fetches from the same EBI edge as ENA/PRIDE, so they are one throughput pool, not three.

free_tier.stated: No fixed quota. Own fair-use policy: 'We place no absolute limit within the 2-month period on the total volume of user data that may exist in a data upload area at any one time' and 'we ... expect that volumes would not exceed 10 Terabytes under normal circumstances.'

retention.stated: Retention: transit area purged after 2 months if not submitted; once submitted, ENA is permanent

egress.terms: Unmetered and anonymous. ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk is CORS-open (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) and already served through Cloudflare (`Server: cloudflare`), so CF is in front by default.

record.tooling: Webin-CLI (github.com/enasequence/webin-cli), plus plain FTP/Aspera. Read side is plain HTTPS/FTP with HTTP range support. Works with rclone's http/`sftp` remotes and curl.
record.chaining: One Webin account = unlimited studies. The upload area is a transit buffer (10 TB documented expectation), while published accessions are permanent and unmetered on the read side. Multiply across accounts/centres; read side needs no account at all, so the fetch workload is uncapped regardless of how many deposit accounts exist.

limits.value: Retention: transit area purged after 2 months

record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none documented per file; per-request volume soft-capped at ~10 TB per 2-month window per upload area, and upload areas are not backed up. Retention: transit area purged after 2 months if not submitted; once submitted, ENA is permanent. Binding constraint on READ is per-ip-shaping: single stream 45 KB/s, 8 parallel ranged GETs 430 KB/s (9.6x).
record.reliability_note: Upload path is the weak side. FTP sessions drop out, Aspera recommended; upload area is explicitly 'not backed up'.
